name: Chao canh
summary: Cháo canh is thick wheat-and-rice noodles in a pork-bone broth cooked until it thickens like porridge. The noodles are firm and chewy, in a glossy yellow broth.
origin: Nghệ An, and a Vinh morning on the city portal’s 24 November 2022 page. Báo Nghệ An, 28 April 2023, also lists it on Đào Tấn.
howToEat: Eat it hot. Vietnamnet, 27 November 2023, blanches the cut noodles, then drops them into boiling water when you order. The broth is pork bone. The add-ins change by place: sliced pork, chả, boiled quail eggs, fish, or shrimp. Cilantro, scallion, and fried shallot go on at the end.
where: VnExpress, 4 September 2016, names the citadel gate at Cửa Nam and Đinh Công Tráng. Báo Nghệ An names the fixed kitchens on Đào Tấn. A lane spelled Hermann on a 3 May 2025 VnExpress page was not given a Vietnamese street name. Check on arrival for that lane. The hour is Check on arrival.
